MISDIRECTED IDEALISM 
COMPLICATING PROBLEM 
No matter how strong and sincere one's desire to serve may 


be, it is by itself not enough when working with people, 


"To make things worse, even the highest ideals and warmest 
concern can be misdirected so they will backfire and compound existing 


difficulties," warns A, Ross Seaman of the Montreal YMCA, 


Mr. Seaman, a veteran youth worker and a member of the Y's 
Metropolitan Program & Field Services staff, suggests that the new pro- 


blems thus created are often more serious than those which nurtured them, 


“People--especially youth--tend to either give up or lash 
out blindly when their efforts to help effect needed change are un- 


acknowledged, misunderstood or dismissed lightly, he emphasizes. 


“Rebuffed by seeming indifference, impatient with adult 
society's apparent lack of humanity, alienated by an ostensible dis- 
position towards impersonalization--some of them turn to anarchy as an 


alternative," 


mend? «hrm 


ay en 


The rising incidence of violence, together with the spreading 
rejection of adult values, have made it clear society is at an important 


crossroads, 


“We can't pass laws to make the problems disappear," says 


Mr. Seaman, "They are real, they are complex and they are here now," 


Unfortunately, some adults have been so angered by acts of 
destruction and indifference that they seem to have resigned themselves 
to just sit back and hope, Many seem to think that young people are 


either destructive militants or passive apathists. 


"They overlook the many thousands of teenagers and young 
adults, in schools and otherwise, who are looking for constructive ways 


to participate in change,'' deplores the YMCA worker. 


He emphasized that this group is in its way also militant, 
It too demands change, attacks injustice and insists on being heard, But 


it rejects anarchy and wants to rebuild, instead of destroy, 


“Part of our job is to join the idealism and energy of 
these young people with the experience and resources of adults in a 


concerted effort to get at the root sources of dissent," says Mr, Seaman, 


"In doing so, we hope to win support from the so-called 
apathists, While usually less ready or able to express themselves than

either the 'destructivists' or ‘constructivists', we do know for sure 
many of them are desperately anxious to get involved."
